senses.definition: Introducing a clause that is the object of a verb, especially a reporting verb or verb expressing belief, knowledge, perception, etc.
examples: He told me that the book is a good read.
I believe that it is true.

senses.definition: Introducing a clause that is the subject of a verb, especially the 'be' verb or a verb expressing judgement, opinion, etc.

examples: It is almost certain that she will come.
It amazes me that people still believe this nonsense.
The boss ordered that the worker enter the room.
That she will come is almost certain.
That people still believe this nonsense amazes me.

senses.definition: Introducing a clause that complements an adjective or passive participle.
examples: I'm sure that you are right.
She is convinced that he is British.

subsenses.definition: Expressing a reason or cause: because, in that.
examples: Be glad that you have enough to eat.

senses.definition: Introducing a subordinate clause modifying an adverb.
examples: Was John there? — Not that I saw.
How often did she visit him? — Twice that I saw.

senses.definition: Introducing a clause that describes the information content of a preceding reporting noun.
examples: I heard a rumour that they got married.
Reports that he left the country are circulating.

senses.definition: Introducing — especially, but not exclusively, with an antecedent like so or such — a subordinate clause expressing a result, consequence, or effect.
examples: The noise was so loud that she woke up.
The problem was sufficiently important that it had to be addressed.
